summary: Connects to a Socket.IO v3/v4 server, listens for configured server events, and emits events to the server from Python.

key_params.name: reset
key_params.note: Disconnect and reconnect the Socket.IO connection

key_params.name: callbacks
key_params.note: Callback DAT executed once for each incoming message or listened event

key_params.name: executeloc
key_params.note: Choose the execution context for received-message callback scripts

key_params.name: fromop
key_params.note: Operator path used when Execute from is set to Specified Operator

key_params.name: maxlines
key_params.note: Maximum number of received message rows to retain

key_params.name: bytes
key_params.note: Output raw bytes in a separate column

key_params.name: customext
key_params.note: Custom editor extension when Extension is set to Custom Extension

key_params.name: extension
key_params.note: Edit/view file extension exposed to external editors

key_params.name: wordwrap
key_params.note: Common DAT node-display word wrap setting

common_gotchas: The four optional inputs have fixed meanings: headers, event names, query parameters, and auth parameters.
Events are emitted with the SocketIO DAT Python emit method; acknowledgement callbacks are not supported.
The DAT uses socket.io C++ Client API v3.1.0 and is intended for socket.io v3 or v4 servers.
TLS verification can fail with self-signed or local certificates unless intentionally configured.
Socket.IO status messages print to the TouchDesigner text console, which may require TOUCH_TEXT_CONSOLE=1 before launch.
key_concepts: Connects to a Socket.IO server and logs messages/events in a DAT.
URL, certificate verification, delay, active, and reset parameters control the connection lifecycle.
Callbacks handle incoming Socket.IO events and messages.
FIFO retention and bytes controls manage event table size and byte display.
